note: Behavior rulings recorded from the source file at the pin, their own wording included. Evidence with zero authority: a ruling becomes contract only when the command it attaches to is activated and the ruling is re-judged affirmatively against the re-derived surface. A command the verb charter deletes takes its rulings with it.

rulings.prior_behavior: the 22-command list ends at `audit` with no registered-vault namespace; GLOBAL OPTIONS lists `--config` and has no `--vault`; the `-C/--cwd` description is truncated at 70 chars with an ellipsis in `--help`
rulings.recorded_behavior: a `vault` namespace (register/unregister/list/set) is listed after `audit`, exposing the ADR 0017 registry; GLOBAL OPTIONS drops `--config` and adds `--vault NAME`; the `-C/--cwd` description is shown in FULL (unclamped) in `--help`, only the concise line in `-h` (NRN-335); the `describe` row's one-line summary names the `--schema` surface the config dump moved behind (NRN-470), so that COMMANDS row's text differs too. A FURTHER difference is normalized away rather than gated here: the rewrite always lists a `self-update` COMMANDS row, while the pinned oracle lists it only where it finds the release-installer receipt it was installed with (present beside a `$HOME` install, absent under the harness's cleared environment and absent from the CI musl artifact) — and accepts the command either way. That row's presence tracks the environment and the build rather than either binary, and an extent is a platform-invariant number, so `Normalization::SelfUpdateCommandRow` removes the row from BOTH sides for this case
rulings.surface: --help (top-level command list + GLOBAL OPTIONS)

rulings.prior_behavior: GLOBAL OPTIONS lists `--config <YAML config file>` and has no `--vault`; `-C/--cwd` is truncated at 70 chars in `--help`; on `find --help`, `--no-limit` reads 'Overrides --limit', `--starts-at` reads '1-indexed ... Default 1', and `--all-cols` reads 'Mutually exclusive with --col'
rulings.recorded_behavior: GLOBAL OPTIONS drops `--config` (config is resolver-derived under ADR 0017) and adds `--vault NAME` (registered-vault targeting the summoner consumes); `-C/--cwd` shows its full description unclamped in `--help` (NRN-335); on `find --help` the Sort-and-paging / Output help text also changes — `--no-limit` and `--all-cols` state last-wins and `--starts-at` states zero-indexing / Default 0 (NRN-331 / NRN-332)
rulings.surface: <command> --help (GLOBAL OPTIONS block)

rulings.prior_behavior: a `^block-id` inside a fenced code block is a real anchor, so `[[code-anchor#^blkincode]]` resolves (a resolved outgoing link)
rulings.recorded_behavior: code is opaque (ADR 0019): the code-fenced `^blkincode` is not an anchor, so the reference is unresolved (block-ref-missing)
rulings.surface: get --col .outgoing_links,.unresolved_links (code-fenced block-id resolution)

rulings.prior_behavior: a leading UTF-8 BOM hides the frontmatter: the block is unrecognized, so its fields are absent and the whole file (fences included) is body
rulings.recorded_behavior: the BOM is skipped before the fence (NRN-349): the frontmatter is recognized and its fields are queryable, and body starts after the closing fence
rulings.surface: get --all-cols (BOM-prefixed frontmatter)

rulings.prior_behavior: `--starts-at` is 1-indexed with a silent floor (`0` and `1` both mean the first record); `--starts-at 1 --limit 1` returns the first document
rulings.recorded_behavior: `--starts-at` is a zero-indexed offset, default 0, no floor; `--starts-at 1 --limit 1` skips the first document and returns the SECOND (NRN-332)
rulings.surface: find --starts-at (paging offset)

rulings.prior_behavior: `--limit N --no-limit` is a hard conflict: the oracle exits 2 with `the argument '--limit <N>' cannot be used with '--no-limit'`
rulings.recorded_behavior: `--limit N --no-limit` is accepted last-wins (NRN-331): `--no-limit` given last wins → unlimited, exit 0. The CLI resolves the order into one wire value; on the wire `no_limit` wins when both arrive
rulings.surface: find --limit / --no-limit (competing flags)

rulings.prior_behavior: decode-then-split: `note%23draft.md` decodes first, so the `#` splits it into target `note` + anchor `draft.md` (unresolved target-missing); `url-block-target.md#^blk1` slugifies `^blk1` as a heading anchor, reported anchor-missing
rulings.recorded_behavior: split-then-decode (NRN-356): the fragment is split off the raw reference before decoding, so `note%23draft.md` stays one path segment named `note#draft.md`; `#^blk1` classifies as a block ref (like the wikilink path) that resolves against the target's `^blk1` block-id (a resolved outgoing link)
rulings.surface: get --col .outgoing_links,.unresolved_links (Markdown-link split-then-decode + block-ref)

rulings.prior_behavior: a hand-rolled lowercase prefix list classifies only `http://`/`https://`/`mailto:`/`#` as external; `tel:`, `file:`, protocol-relative `//`, a `C:/…` drive letter, and mixed-case `hTTp://` all fall through as local links, reported unresolved (target-missing)
rulings.recorded_behavior: URL-rules classification (NRN-357): any case-insensitive RFC 3986 scheme, a protocol-relative `//`, or a Windows drive-letter path is external and excluded from the link model, so none of these destinations appear as links at all; a destination whose first segment contains a colon (e.g. `note:draft.md`) also reads as scheme-qualified and classifies external — disambiguate a literal colon-named vault file with a `./` prefix
rulings.surface: get --col .outgoing_links,.unresolved_links (external-vs-local scheme classification)

rulings.prior_behavior: a user error prints an unprefixed, terse line to stderr: `no document matched: <t>`, `unknown --col facet '.x' (valid facets: …)`, `invalid config <path>: unknown field …`, `unknown field `titel` — did you mean `title`? (…)` — no `norn:` prefix, no did-you-mean/hint split, no next-step hint
rulings.recorded_behavior: every user error is a soft landing (NRN-361): a stable `norn:`-prefixed headline (`norn: no document matched path or stem: <t>`, `norn: invalid config <path>: …`, `norn: unknown field `titel``) plus, where a near-miss exists, a leading/standalone did-you-mean `hint:` line (`unknown --col facet '.headngs' — did you mean '.headings'? …`; `hint: did you mean `title`?`) — via the one `closest` heuristic. The unknown-dynamic-field rejection (NRN-367) is this same surface now that the owner-side gate is wired live. stdout stays payload-only in every format
rulings.surface: read-verb error surface (stderr diagnostics: prefix + wording + hints)

rulings.prior_behavior: a repeated scalar flag is a hard conflict: `find --limit 5 --limit 1` exits 2 with `error: the argument '--limit <N>' cannot be used multiple times`, nothing on stdout
rulings.recorded_behavior: a repeated scalar flag is last-wins (NRN-365, `args_override_self` on the root propagated to every subcommand): `find --limit 5 --limit 1` resolves to limit 1, exit 0, the single sorted path on stdout
rulings.surface: repeated scalar flag (grammar-wide last-wins)

rulings.prior_behavior: the per-kind warning object is inconsistent across verbs/kinds: `new` emits `{ "field": "bogus", "kind": "unknown-field" }` (a `kind` discriminator, no message), and other kinds carried different member sets
rulings.recorded_behavior: one unified envelope for every warning kind (NRN-388): `{ "code": "unknown-field", "field": "bogus", "message": "field 'bogus' not declared in schema" }` — a stable kebab `code`, the optional scoped `field`, and an operator-facing `message` (see `crates/norn-wire/src/mutate.rs`, `MutationWarning`)
rulings.surface: set/new --format json warning object (unified envelope)

rulings.prior_behavior: a field `set` against a frontmatter block that parses to YAML null (a bare `null`/`~` scalar block, or a comment-only block) is refused: `error: frontmatter is not a top-level mapping`, exit 2, the document unchanged
rulings.recorded_behavior: the null block promotes to an empty mapping (NRN-371) and the field splices in, exit 0, the tree mutated (a comment-only block keeps its comment and gains the field after it) — a valid input yielding a valid output, closing the new→set null-frontmatter roundtrip (see `crates/norn-frontmatter/src/frontmatter/edit.rs`)
rulings.surface: set against a null-/comment-only frontmatter block (mapping promotion)

rulings.prior_behavior: a change op whose `fields.operation` disagrees with its `kind` silently dispatches by `operation`, executing a different operation than the reviewed `kind` declares — `kind: set_frontmatter` + `operation: remove_frontmatter` runs a REMOVE (here tripping `error: cannot minimal-edit frontmatter for notes/alpha.md: field priority not present in frontmatter`, exit 2)
rulings.recorded_behavior: the mismatch is refused before any dispatch: `error: op.fields.operation 'remove_frontmatter' conflicts with op.kind 'set_frontmatter'`, exit 2, write-free — a reviewed plan must execute as its `kind` declares, so silent reinterpretation is removed
rulings.surface: apply (authored plan: change op `kind` vs `fields.operation` mismatch)

rulings.prior_behavior: every malformed-plan refusal flattens to `code: internal-error` (the typed error is discarded, so the envelope cannot distinguish a malformed plan from a norn bug): the unknown-kind and missing-field cases report `internal-error` with their specific message, and a wrong-typed member (`"operation": 5`) reports `internal-error` with the bare serde decode text
rulings.recorded_behavior: the typed error survives to the envelope: an unknown op kind reports `code: unknown-operation-kind`, and the missing-field / non-object / kind-operation-mismatch / wrong-typed-member family reports `code: malformed-plan` — a machine-branchable signal that the plan, not norn, is at fault. Exit 2 unchanged; the unknown-kind and missing-field messages are unchanged, and a wrong-typed-member decode failure additionally names the kind (`op.fields for <kind> could not be decoded: <serde text>`)
rulings.surface: apply --format json (malformed authored-plan refusal code)

rulings.prior_behavior:
the section body start is the byte after the heading marker's first newline: on a SETEXT heading it lands on the underline, so `replace_section` deletes the underline (`Alpha
-----
Body` → `Alpha
REPLACED.`) and `insert_after_heading` inserts above it (the underline then applies to the inserted line); on a heading at EOF with no trailing newline (`## Tail`) the empty section runs to EOF, so `replace_section`, `append_to_section`, and `insert_after_heading` all weld their content onto the marker (`## Tail` + `NEW.` → `## TailNEW.`; `## Tail` + `- item` → `## Tail- item`)
rulings.recorded_behavior:
the body start is the parser's heading-construct end (past the SETEXT underline), and an op inserting body content after a heading with no trailing newline emits the missing line terminator first (NRN-437): the SETEXT underline is preserved (`Alpha
-----
REPLACED.` / the inserted line lands below the underline) and the EOF heading stays a heading (`## Tail
NEW.` / `## Tail
- item`) — a valid CommonMark heading survives the edit
rulings.surface: edit (section ops on SETEXT / heading-at-EOF body shapes)

rulings.prior_behavior: the cascade rewrites an embed backlink with a `raw.strip_prefix("[[")` that misses the leading `!` of `![[…]]`: the inner collapses and the whole embed is replaced by a bare wikilink, dropping the `!` AND the `|alias` (`![[embed-target|Display]]` → `[[embed-moved]]` on a move; → `[[redirect-target]]` on a delete redirect)
rulings.recorded_behavior: the cascade rebuilds the link through the parser (`reconstruct_wikilink`), preserving the embed marker and the alias: `![[embed-target|Display]]` → `![[embed-moved|Display]]` (move) / `![[redirect-target|Display]]` (delete redirect)
rulings.surface: move / delete --rewrite-to (backlink cascade over an embed reference)

rulings.prior_behavior: the rewriters are not code-opaque: with a fenced `[[fence-target]]` sample ABOVE the real prose backlink, the move cascade's `replacen(raw, .., 1)` rewrites the FIRST file occurrence (the fenced sample) and leaves the real prose link dangling, and the rewrite-wikilink verb's whole-file `find("[[")` scan rewrites BOTH the fenced sample and the prose link
rulings.recorded_behavior: both route through the code-aware parser (`parse_wikilinks`), which excludes fenced / inline-code ranges (ADR 0019): the fenced sample is never touched and only the real prose backlink is rewritten
rulings.surface: move / rewrite-wikilink (a code-fence-shadowed backlink)

rulings.prior_behavior: `split_target_suffix` splits the target at the first `#` OR `^`, but a bare `^` is an ordinary filename character per the parser (a block ref is `#^id`). So `rewrite-wikilink 'a^b' caret-renamed` matches the pre-`^` fragment `a` against the target `a^b`, never rewrites, and leaves `[[a^b]]` untouched while reporting success
rulings.recorded_behavior: matching uses the parser's decomposition (split on `#` only), so the whole `a^b` target matches and `[[a^b]]` is rewritten to `[[caret-renamed]]`
rulings.surface: rewrite-wikilink (a target stem carrying a bare `^`)

rulings.prior_behavior: the ad-hoc rewriters preserve a link's interior whitespace verbatim, inconsistently: a move cascade over `[[spaced-target | Display Name]]` drops the target-side space but keeps the alias-side space (`[[spaced-moved| Display Name]]`), and `rewrite-wikilink` over `[[ padded-target ]]` matches its untrimmed `bare_target` against the trimmed plan target, so it never rewrites and leaves the link untouched while reporting success
rulings.recorded_behavior: the reconstructed link emits the parser-trimmed target and alias, canonicalizing interior whitespace: `[[spaced-target | Display Name]]` → `[[spaced-moved|Display Name]]`, and `[[ padded-target ]]` matches on the trimmed target and rewrites to `[[padded-renamed]]` (the phantom no-op is fixed)
rulings.surface: move / rewrite-wikilink (a backlink with interior whitespace)

rulings.prior_behavior: a rename whose new target carries a `|`/`#`/`[`/`]` is emitted verbatim, so the backlink re-parses as a different link and is silently corrupted: `[[unrepr-target]]` becomes `[[a|b]]` (which reads as target `a`, alias `b`) on both the rewrite-wikilink verb (exit 0) and the move cascade (exit 0)
rulings.recorded_behavior: the target is checked for representability first: the rewrite-wikilink verb REFUSES the whole op (exit 2, `unrepresentable-rewrite-target`, write-free) and the move cascade SKIPS the backlink (`would-corrupt-wikilink`), leaving `[[unrepr-target]]` intact and detectable by `validate` rather than corrupted
rulings.surface: rewrite-wikilink / move (rename to an unrepresentable wikilink target)

rulings.prior_behavior: a present-but-wrong-typed op field is silently coerced to a default: `move_document`'s `"force": "true"` (a string) becomes `false` (then refusing `move destination already exists`, exit 2); `delete_document`'s `"rewrite_to": 5` (a number) is dropped to no-redirect, DELETING the document with its backlinks left broken (exit 0, mutating); `str_replace`'s `"document_hash": 5` becomes `""` (no compare-and-swap), then refusing `string not found` (exit 2) — the malformed field is invisible in every case
rulings.recorded_behavior: each wrong-typed field refuses at plan decode with `code: malformed-plan` and a message naming the field (`op.fields for <kind> could not be decoded: field \`force\` must be a boolean` / `field \`rewrite_to\` must be a string` / `invalid type: integer \`5\`, expected a string`), exit 2, write-free — a reviewed plan never executes on a coerced value, so the delete-with-typo data loss the oracle silently applies is refused
rulings.surface: apply (authored plan: wrong-typed op field — strict decode)

rulings.prior_behavior: each finding serializes an untagged per-variant body flattened onto `{code, severity, path, message}`: a link finding embeds the whole internal `link` model (raw, kind, spans, source_context, resolved_path, unresolved_reason, status, and `candidates` as path objects); a frontmatter finding emits its variant fields (`rule` even when `null`, `field`, plus `allowed_values` / `actual_value` / `max_length` / `allowed_paths` / … as applicable) — an output shape that is an accident of internal representation
rulings.recorded_behavior: each finding serializes the flat closed contract `{ path, code, severity, message, rule?, field?, value?, target?, candidates?, next_actions? }`: `path`-first field order on the struct itself and on `--format jsonl` (the `--format json` envelope and the MCP structuredContent re-serialize through a sorted map, so their keys are alphabetical), absent optionals omitted rather than `null`, `candidates` as plain vault-path strings, no internal `link` / diagnostic model and no variant-specific frontmatter fields — the detail that carried fix-vs-skip value folded into `message`, the rest dropped EXCEPT the offending value, retained as the contract's universal optional `value` slot (populated by `value-not-allowed` / `field-type-invalid` / `frontmatter-forbidden-field`, and for an element-wise `value-not-allowed` carrying the single violating element; `frontmatter-exceeds-max-length` is excluded, its message already naming both lengths)
rulings.surface: validate --format json / jsonl + vault.validate (per-finding shape)

rulings.prior_behavior: an unparseable predicate value is accepted silently at exit 0: a non-`today` date value passes verbatim into a TEXT lexical compare (`--before created:yesterday` → `created < 'yesterday'`, which matches every stored ISO date), and a malformed `--path` glob (`{unclosed`) has its parse error discarded so it filters out every document (an empty result set, indistinguishable from a real no-match)
rulings.recorded_behavior: each unparseable predicate input refuses at `build_document_query` with exit 2: a date value that is neither `today` nor a valid ISO 8601 date/datetime reports `invalid --before date value 'yesterday': expected \`today\`, an ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD), or an ISO 8601 datetime`, and a malformed `--path` glob reports `invalid --path glob '{unclosed': <reason>` — no silently-wrong or silently-empty result set
rulings.surface: find/count query predicate input validation (date value + --path glob)

rulings.prior_behavior: value-comparison predicates eager-type the token before SQL: `--eq zip:07030` coerces to the integer 7030, which never equals the stored string "07030" (zero results, exit 0 — a silent miss); `--not-eq zip:07030` likewise finds "07030" != 7030 and returns the doc the user meant to exclude; a non-ISO value on a value operator against a declared-date field lexically compares as a string (zero results, exit 0)
rulings.recorded_behavior: the schema is the type authority where declared and undeclared/disagreeing fields dual-type: `--eq zip:07030` matches either the string "07030" or the number 7030 (returns alpha); `--not-eq zip:07030` excludes either representation (drops alpha, returns every other doc; docs missing the field stay included); a value-comparison predicate on the declared-date `due` field with a non-ISO value refuses at exit 2 naming the field, the declared type, and the value
rulings.surface: find value-comparison predicate typing (--eq/--not-eq on quoted numeric; declared-date refusal)

rulings.prior_behavior: every one of these refusals flattens to `code: internal-error` (the bare `anyhow` carries no typed code, so the apply envelope cannot distinguish a malformed plan from a norn bug): a create into an existing destination, a create into a missing parent dir, a create with a non-object `new_value.frontmatter`, an owner-set precondition with an empty stem selector, and two ops sharing an id all report `internal-error` with their specific message and no `path`
rulings.recorded_behavior: each refusal carries a typed, machine-branchable code: `create-destination-exists` and `create-parent-missing` (both additionally echoing the offending vault-relative `path`), `malformed-plan` for the non-object frontmatter and the duplicate op id, and `invalid-precondition` for the empty stem selector — `internal-error` is reserved for genuine norn defects. Exit 2 and every message are unchanged
rulings.surface: apply --format json (bare-anyhow user-fault refusal codes)

rulings.prior_behavior: the report reconstructs per-op status from the event log and under-counts: op0 is mis-marked `skipped` and the created-doc lockstep hands its resolved path to op1, so the summary reads `applied: 1  skipped: 1` with BOTH create lines printing `create seq/task-1.md` — `seq/task-2.md` never appears — despite both files landing on disk
rulings.recorded_behavior: the applier records each op's outcome as it happens, so the report tells the truth: `applied: 2  skipped: 0` with the two distinct resolved summaries `create seq/task-1.md` and `create seq/task-2.md` — matching the (unchanged) post-state
rulings.surface: apply --yes (multi-seq-create report: true per-op status vs event reconstruction)

rulings.prior_behavior: the applier aborts the whole plan at the first per-op failure: op0 `applied`, op1 `failed` (create-parent-missing), op2 `not_run` — `applied: 1  remaining: 1`, exit 1 — and only `nrn406-first.md` lands on disk
rulings.recorded_behavior: the failed op is recorded and INDEPENDENT ops still run: op0 `applied`, op1 `failed`, op2 `applied` — `applied: 2  remaining: 0`, exit 1 — and both `nrn406-first.md` and `nrn406-third.md` land on disk (a truthful partial apply)
rulings.surface: apply --yes (independent files proceed after a per-op failure)

rulings.prior_behavior: a `delete_document` op with no `document_hash` is accepted: the delete forecasts `outcome: applied` (exit 0) and, confirmed, removes the file with no compare-and-swap against its bytes
rulings.recorded_behavior: the op is refused fail-closed: `code: delete-hash-required` naming the offending path (exit 2), at a plan-level barrier before any write — a delete must carry the plan-time hash it will compare-and-swap
rulings.surface: apply --format json (hand-authored hash-less delete refusal)

rulings.prior_behavior: a `move_document` op is never fingerprinted, so a plan-time `document_hash` that no longer matches the source is ignored: the move forecasts `outcome: applied` (exit 0) and, confirmed, renames the drifted file anyway
rulings.recorded_behavior: a present `document_hash` is a pre-rename compare-and-swap: a stale hash refuses `stale-document-hash` (exit 2) before the rename, the same drift-refusal class the delete and content paths already enforce (an absent hash still proceeds unchecked)
rulings.surface: apply --format json (move stale-hash refusal — the new optional move CAS)

rulings.prior_behavior: the section resolver requires the bare heading text: a `replace_section` anchored on the natural markdown form `## Section One` refuses `heading not found: "## Section One"` (exit 2), write-free
rulings.recorded_behavior: the resolver tries the anchor exactly, then strips a leading ATX prefix (and any trailing closer) on the miss and matches on heading TEXT (level is syntax noise): `## Section One` resolves the `Section One` section and the edit applies (exit 0)
rulings.surface: edit --yes (forgiving ATX-prefixed heading anchor)

rulings.prior_behavior: an ambiguous stem prints `note: '<stem>' resolved to N docs` — an off-set prefix, and a message that counts the collisions without naming one — and an unresolved `--col` field prints `warn: --col field '<f>' not present ...`, a second prefix outside the closed set
rulings.recorded_behavior: both render on the closed `warning:` prefix: the ambiguity is a `warning`-severity typed note and the `--col`/`--sort` annotation speaks the one closed vocabulary. The ambiguity note's TEXT also changes, on the same line: it is now the shared resolver wording `ambiguous document stem: <stem>; candidates: <a>, <b>` (NRN-467, PD-467), naming the colliding paths instead of counting them, so the reader disambiguates without a second query. stdout / exit / post-state unchanged; the stderr prefix and that message text are the whole divergence
rulings.surface: get (stderr annotation prefix — closed note/warning/error vocabulary)

rulings.prior_behavior: a not-run op label is the `Debug`-lowercased variant, printing `[notrun]` (hyphen-free) — a label that does not match the status's kebab wire value
rulings.recorded_behavior: the label is the serde-kebab name, printing `[not-run]` — the same string as the `OpStatus::NotRun` wire value; only this records-body label diverges (exit 2, write-free on both)
rulings.surface: apply (records — not-run op/precondition status label)

rulings.prior_behavior: `structuredContent.notes` is an array of prose strings (e.g. `"error: '<t>' did not resolve to any doc"`); a client recovers severity only by matching the `error:` prefix, and the message is `get`'s own phrasing for a failed resolution
rulings.recorded_behavior: `structuredContent.notes` is an array of typed `{severity, code, message}` objects, and the note's `message` is the shared resolver wording `no document matched path or stem: <t>` (NRN-467, PD-467) rather than a `get`-local phrasing; the `isError: true` bit is unchanged (derived from the `error`-severity note), so the notes payload — its shape and that one message — is the whole divergence
rulings.surface: mcp vault.get (structuredContent.notes — typed severity notes)

rulings.prior_behavior: the oracle has a service-local `--vault <PATH>` and no global `--vault`: `service status --vault <path>` recognizes the local flag and fails canonicalizing a nonexistent path (exit 1, `vault root could not be canonicalized: ...`); `--vault <name> service status` is an unrecognized argument before any subcommand parses (exit 2, `error: unexpected argument '--vault' found`)
rulings.recorded_behavior: the service-local `--vault <PATH>` is deleted (NRN-417); `--vault` is unambiguously the global `Option<String>` NAME selector (ADR 0017) everywhere, which `service` never consults: both orderings now parse cleanly and reach the same uniform not-yet-ported outcome (exit 1, `` `service` is not yet ported in this build ``) — a wholly different stderr in both cases, and a different exit code (1, not 2) in the before-subcommand ordering
rulings.surface: service status (--vault flag collision: local flag deleted, ADR 0017 global selector only)

rulings.prior_behavior: the JSON shape is a per-verb zoo: an applied `set --format json` is compact (single line, no indentation); a `set` refusal is a bare pretty `{code,message}` fragment with no report envelope; `new` and `edit` refuse as bare `error: <message>` prose on stderr even under `--format json`; and a `move` refusal is a bare pretty `{code,message}` fragment — four different refusal shapes across the mutation verbs
rulings.recorded_behavior: every mutation verb's `--format json` emits the FULL report envelope on every outcome path, pretty-printed in serde struct-field order with one trailing newline: an applied `set` report is now pretty rather than compact, and every refusal (`set` / `new` / `edit` / `move`) carries the whole report (`outcome: refused` plus the coded error in its failed op / `error` field) instead of a bare fragment or bare prose — one shape a consumer parses on every verb and outcome; exit codes are unchanged (2 on refusal, 0 otherwise). Inside that envelope, the three target-resolution refusals here (`set` / `edit` / `move`) also carry the shared resolver wording `no document matched path or stem: <t>` (NRN-467, PD-467) in place of each verb's own phrasing — a second cause on the same differing region, not a separate one
rulings.surface: mutation-report --format json (one serializer policy: full envelope, pretty, struct order, trailing newline)

rulings.prior_behavior: a `set` / `new` / `edit` dry-run forecast reports `outcome: applied` while `applied: false` — a self-contradiction (there is no separate `dry_run` field), so a consumer keying on `outcome` sees a preview as a completed write; the `edit --format json` forecast additionally serializes compact
rulings.recorded_behavior: a forecast reports `outcome: forecast` (present-tense honest, distinct from a confirmed `applied`), on both the CLI `edit --dry-run --format json` (now also pretty per PD-135) and the MCP `vault.set` forecast `structuredContent`; a consumer tells a preview from a real write by `outcome` alone
rulings.surface: set/new/edit forecast outcome (MutationOutcome::Forecast — dry-run reports outcome: forecast)

rulings.prior_behavior: `structuredContent` carries only `{plan, has_diagnostic_errors}`; a client re-derives the per-code finding tally itself and cannot see a skipped finding's candidate paths or next actions
rulings.recorded_behavior: `structuredContent` carries the deterministic `plan` plus `findings_by_code` / `findings_total` / `total_docs` and the rich `skipped_detail` (reason code, candidate paths, operator next-actions per skipped finding — the ADR 0024 first-consumer surface); the plan's non-deterministic `generated_at` is the only field the harness normalizes
rulings.surface: mcp vault.repair (structuredContent — richer RepairReport + rich skip detail)

rulings.prior_behavior: the oracle grounds the `-C` path and fails at the low-level canonicalize call: `vault root could not be canonicalized: <path>: No such file or directory (os error 2)` on stderr, exit 1
rulings.recorded_behavior: the rewrite's client-side precheck refuses instantly before summoning any owner: `norn: vault root does not exist: <path> (from -C)` on stderr — naming the actual path and the via — exit 1, no owner spawned and no socket dialed
rulings.surface: read verbs with a missing -C vault root (client-side precheck, instant refusal)

rulings.prior_behavior: an ambiguous `delete <stem>` refuses `target-ambiguous` with `document resolves ambiguously by stem: <stem> → []` — the candidate set is dropped before the message is built, so the message names none of the colliding documents
rulings.recorded_behavior: the same refusal renders the REAL sorted candidate paths, threaded through a structured `TargetResolution::Ambiguous`, so a caller sees exactly which documents collide. The whole message is also the shared resolver wording every verb now speaks (NRN-467, PD-467) — `ambiguous document stem: duplicate; candidates: archive2/duplicate.md, notes/duplicate.md` — replacing both `delete`'s own `document resolves ambiguously by stem: … → …` phrasing and the Rust `Debug` rendering of the candidate vector, so the list reads as prose rather than as a quoted array literal; code / exit / write-free behavior unchanged
rulings.surface: delete ambiguous-stem refusal (records) — real candidate paths in the message

rulings.prior_behavior: the `--col field ... not present in any matching document` warning fires even on a `--limit`-truncated page (a field present only beyond the page boundary false-positives) and on a zero-match result (every field is trivially absent) — the same false positive `--sort` was already fixed against
rulings.recorded_behavior: the bare-field warning returns early when the page is truncated (`returned < total`) or the match set is empty, so it fires only when every matching document was actually inspected and genuinely lacks the field; the unknown-facet check stays unconditional
rulings.surface: find/get --col unknown-field warning (guarded to a full, non-empty result set)

rulings.prior_behavior: the full `tools/list` catalog is 14 tools, none of which constrains `additionalProperties`, so an unknown param key is silently ignored. `get`'s `inputSchema` documents `starts_at` as a 1-indexed default (`default: 1`), matching the oracle's paging, and its `format` enum accepts `structured` / `markdown`. Six other tools publish param shapes that do not mirror the oracle's own CLI flags: `find.col` is a string ARRAY (`default: []`) where `--col` takes one comma-separated token, and `find.starts_at` is `integer|null` (`default: null`); `new` takes `vars` as a KEY->VALUE OBJECT (`default: {}`) where `--var` is a repeatable `KEY=VALUE` token; `rewrite_wikilink` names its two required params `from` / `to` where the CLI positionals are `<OLD>` / `<NEW>`; `repair` takes `confidence` as a nullable `ConfidenceBand` enum `$def` and leaves its eight filter arrays with no declared default; `audit` takes `status` as an `AuditStatusFilter` enum `$def` (`applied` / `skipped` / `failed`) and `limit` as `integer|null` (`default: null`); `edit` types `edits` as an array of the `EditOp` union `$def` and lists it as REQUIRED alongside `target`
rulings.recorded_behavior: the catalog is the same 14 tools, but every one publishes `additionalProperties: false` — each param struct declares `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown key is refused instead of ignored. `get`'s `inputSchema` documents `starts_at` as a zero-indexed default (`default: 0`, NRN-332) — the MCP-surface face of PD-105 — and its `format` enum accepts `records` / `markdown`, the CLI's own `--format` value names (NRN-469; the call-surface face is PD-469). The six other tools' params now mirror the CLI flags they stand for, which is an MCP-surface-only change on each (the CLI flags themselves are identical on both binaries, so no CLI-side entry covers them): `find.col` is `string|null` (`default: null`), one comma-separated token like `--col`, and `find.starts_at` is a plain `integer` (`default: 0`, the same PD-105 redesign); `new` takes `var` as an ARRAY of `KEY=VALUE` tokens (`default: []`), matching repeatable `--var`; `rewrite_wikilink`'s required params are `old` / `new`, matching the `<OLD>` / `<NEW>` positionals; `repair` takes `confidence_high` as a plain bool (`default: false`) in place of the enum `$def`, and its eight filter arrays declare `default: []`; `audit` takes `status` as `string|null` (`default: null`) in place of the enum `$def`, and `limit` as a plain `integer` (`default: 20`, the CLI's own `--limit` default); `edit` leaves `edits` untyped (`default: null`) and requires only `target`. The remaining delta is prose — tool descriptions, the filter-predicate descriptions the three read tools publish from one definition, and the typed-note schemas PD-133 covers on the call surface
rulings.surface: mcp tools/list (published inputSchema — param strictness, get.starts_at / get.format, and six tools' param shapes)

rulings.prior_behavior: the page opens with the long-about body (op reference, heading-addressing / safety / exit-code paragraphs) before USAGE; OPTIONS lists `--ops-file <PATH>` despite the flag being declared `hide = true`; `--yes` reads 'Apply the edits without an interactive confirm prompt', `--dry-run` reads 'Preview the edits without writing', and `--format` reads 'Output format'; GLOBAL OPTIONS lists `--config <YAML config file>`, truncates `-C/--cwd` at 70 chars, and has no `--vault`
rulings.recorded_behavior: the page's description prose is one paragraph stating the transactional contract the two entry paths (`--edits-json` or the sugar flags) share — an ordered op array applied all-or-nothing, each op against the result of the prior, any anchor failure refusing the whole batch — in place of the oracle's op reference and its heading-addressing / safety / exit-code paragraphs (the earned-prose disposition in PD-461); OPTIONS omits `--ops-file` entirely — a command-local hidden arg is filtered the same way a hidden global already was; `--yes` and `--dry-run` use the verb-neutral 'the change' wording every mutation verb shares and `--format` reads 'Output format; `json` emits the mutation-report envelope' (NRN-416); GLOBAL OPTIONS drops `--config`, shows `-C/--cwd` in full, and adds `--vault NAME` (the PD-102 reshape)
rulings.surface: edit --help (whole page: long-about, OPTIONS, GLOBAL OPTIONS)

rulings.prior_behavior: a cascade-verb (`move` / `delete` / `rewrite-wikilink` / `apply`) dry-run reports `outcome: applied` alongside `dry_run: true` — a consumer keying on `outcome` sees a preview as a completed write, and preview detection is per-verb-family (`forecast` for `set`/`new`/`edit`, `dry_run` for the cascade verbs)
rulings.recorded_behavior: a clean cascade dry-run reports `outcome: forecast` (present-tense honest, distinct from a confirmed `applied`), on both the CLI `--dry-run --format json` `ApplyReport` and the MCP `vault.move` / `vault.delete` forecast result; the `dry_run: true` flag is retained and now consistent with `outcome`, so `outcome == "forecast"` is one preview signal across all seven mutation verbs. Exit codes and the applied/skipped/failed counts are unchanged
rulings.surface: move/delete/rewrite-wikilink/apply forecast outcome (ApplyOutcome::Forecast — cascade dry-run reports outcome: forecast)

rulings.prior_behavior: bare `repair --format json` ignores `--format` and prints the human prose findings summary (`N findings across M documents`, the per-code tally, the repairable/skipped line, and the apply-guidance lines) — identical bytes to a bare `repair` with no `--format`
rulings.recorded_behavior: bare `repair --format json` emits the findings-summary report envelope as JSON — `findings_total`, `total_docs`, the sorted `findings_by_code` tally, and the `operations`/`skipped` counts — the JSON of what the bare invocation prints without `--format`, never the MigrationPlan (that stays `--plan --format json`)
rulings.surface: repair --format json (bare, no --plan — findings-summary report envelope)

rulings.prior_behavior: the OPTIONS block has no `--no-pager` flag (`get` has no pager at all); `--no-limit` reads 'Overrides --limit', `--starts-at` reads '1-indexed ... Default 1', and `--all-cols` reads 'Mutually exclusive with `--col`'; GLOBAL OPTIONS lists `--config <YAML config file>`, truncates `-C/--cwd` at 70 chars, and has no `--vault`
rulings.recorded_behavior: the OPTIONS block lists `--no-pager` ("Skip the pager even when stdout is a TTY") — `get` pages its `records` and `markdown` output on a TTY exactly like `find` pages its `records` output; `--no-limit` and `--all-cols` state last-wins and `--starts-at` states zero-indexing / Default 0 (NRN-331 / NRN-332); GLOBAL OPTIONS drops `--config`, shows `-C/--cwd` in full, and adds `--vault NAME` (the PD-102 reshape)
rulings.surface: get --help (whole page: OPTIONS, paging/projection text, GLOBAL OPTIONS)

rulings.prior_behavior: `new` never enforces allowed_values before writing: a `--field status=someday` outside the matching rule's allowed set passes type coercion, the create APPLIES (exit 0, file written), and the violation surfaces only as a non-blocking `value-not-allowed` warning from the post-create validate pass — and only on a confirmed apply, so a forecast reports clean
rulings.recorded_behavior: the synthesized frontmatter is validated for allowed_values at forecast/preflight: a value outside the schema's allowed set REFUSES (`value-not-allowed`, exit 2, write-free). The allowed set is the INTERSECTION of every co-applying rule that declares the field (NRN-474), not one rule's list, so rule order carries no weight; it is carried both in the refusal message and in the envelope's structured `allowed` recovery slot (NRN-473). `--force` bypasses to a `force-bypass` warning and applies. Enforcement is identical on the CLI `norn new` and the MCP `vault.new` (one owner seam)
rulings.surface: new allowed_values enforcement (schema-violating create refuses at preflight; --force bypasses)

rulings.prior_behavior: `allowed_values` matches an array-valued field WHOLE against the configured scalar set — `frontmatter_value_matches` has no `(Array, String)` arm, so the match never succeeds and every array value on a constrained field reports `value-not-allowed`, even when every element is in the set
rulings.recorded_behavior: `allowed_values` matches an array-valued field ELEMENT-WISE — one finding per violating element, none when every element is allowed (an empty array yields no findings). Each element finding names the offending element in its message (`… disallowed value: tags (element: bogus)`) and carries it in the `value` slot, so siblings on one field are distinguishable (NRN-476); a scalar field is unaffected, matching whole with its message unchanged
rulings.surface: validate (allowed_values on a list_of_strings field — element-wise match)

rulings.prior_behavior: `get bee` resolves via the alias fallback (`notes/beta.md` declares `aliases: [bee]`; stem `bee` does not exist) and returns the beta record
rulings.recorded_behavior: `get`'s resolution ladder is path → stem only (NRN-455); `bee` matches no path or stem, so `get bee` resolves to no doc and emits a `target-not-found` error note. `aliases` stays queryable via `find`
rulings.surface: get <alias> (target resolution — alias fallback removed)

rulings.prior_behavior: `notes/gamma.md`'s `[[bee]]` resolves via `notes/beta.md`'s alias, so it is not a finding; the link-target-missing set and warning tally exclude it (the zoo fixture carries the `beta`/`gamma` alias pair; `Profile::alias_link`, `crate::zoo::valid_docs`)
rulings.recorded_behavior: aliases do not participate in resolution (NRN-455), so `[[bee]]` is `link-target-missing` on `notes/gamma.md` — one more warning-severity finding, one more affected path, and a higher warning tally than the oracle reports. The `clean` profile omits the alias pair entirely (`Profile::alias_link` is false there) so its finding-free invariant holds under the rewrite too — only the zoo fixture demonstrates this divergence
rulings.surface: validate (alias-only wikilink now dangling — zoo fixture)

rulings.prior_behavior: the oracle resolves `notes/gamma.md`'s `[[bee]]` via alias, so repair sees no finding for it and proposes no operation
rulings.recorded_behavior: `[[bee]]` is dangling and uniquely matches `notes/beta.md`'s alias, so repair plans a built-in `rewrite_link` op (`bee` → the `beta` stem, `built-in:alias-stem`, alias-suggestion footnote) — one more finding, one more planned operation, and `notes/gamma.md` in the affected paths (NRN-455). The `clean` profile omits the alias pair (`Profile::alias_link` is false there), so it stays finding-free and this entry no longer needs to cover it
rulings.surface: repair (alias-only dangling link + deterministic alias-hint — zoo fixture)

rulings.prior_behavior: `find --all-cols` on the zoo emits `notes/gamma.md`'s `[[bee]]` among its resolved outgoing links (the oracle resolves it via alias)
rulings.recorded_behavior: aliases do not participate in resolution (NRN-455), so `notes/gamma.md`'s `[[bee]]` renders as an unresolved link in the all-columns projection instead of a resolved one
rulings.surface: find --all-cols (link-resolution columns expose the dangling alias link)

rulings.prior_behavior: `describe --format json` serializes the whole describe report regardless of what a bare `describe` prints: `folders` as the full directory array, `path_rules` / `creatable_rules` as full objects carrying their `frontmatter_defaults`, `inbox`, and `schema` as the entire validate config
rulings.recorded_behavior: `describe --format json` is the JSON projection of the records block — `folders` / `path_rules` / `creatable_rules` as integer COUNTS, `inbox` (`null` when unconfigured), and `data` only when a contents-summary was requested (`--data`/`--stats`/`--by`). The full declared config is reachable as `describe --schema`, whose `--format json` emits exactly the payload the oracle's bare `--format json` emitted, and whose records rendering prints the same sections human-legibly
rulings.surface: describe --format json (records-summary projection vs whole-config dump)

rulings.prior_behavior: a zero count drops its line entirely (the zoo prints `folders`/`path rules` only — no `creatable` line, since the fixture declares no creatable rule) and an unconfigured `inbox.path` prints no `inbox` line at all, so a reader cannot tell a zero from an omission
rulings.recorded_behavior: all four count lines print on every invocation — `folders`, `path rules`, `creatable`, `inbox` — with `0` where the count is zero and `(none)` where no `inbox.path` is configured. The contents-summary block that follows under `--data`/`--stats`/`--by` is unchanged; only the structure block ahead of it gains lines
rulings.surface: describe (records — the structure counts block prints zeros and an absent inbox)

rulings.prior_behavior: the page prints the internal doc comment of the shared `FilterArgs` struct as `count`'s description — two paragraphs about `cli.rs`, `build.rs`, intra-crate deps, and where `build_document_query` lives — between the one-line summary and USAGE; `--format` reads 'Output format. Default text (records-block)' over 'Possible values: text, json'; GLOBAL OPTIONS lists `--config <YAML config file>`, truncates `-C/--cwd` at 70 chars, and has no `--vault`
rulings.recorded_behavior: the page prints the one-line summary and goes straight to USAGE: all five flattened arg groups (`GlobalArgs`, `MutationModeArgs`, `ValidateTriageArgs`, `FilterArgs`, `SortPaginateArgs`) carry plain comments clap cannot adopt, so no source-tree text can reach a help page, and description prose is kept only where it decides something the flags, EXAMPLES, and conceptual sections do not — `get`, `validate`, `edit`, and `self-update` — dropped on the other 17 paths that carry it on the oracle; `--format` reads 'Output format. Default records (records-block)' over 'Possible values: records, json' (the converged format vocabulary, NRN-416); GLOBAL OPTIONS drops `--config`, shows `-C/--cwd` in full, and adds `--vault NAME` (the PD-102 reshape)
rulings.surface: count --help (whole page: description prose / long_about, OUTPUT --format, GLOBAL OPTIONS)

rulings.prior_behavior: `format: "records"` is an unknown variant: the call fails deserialization with `isError: true` and a text-only content reading ``failed to deserialize parameters: unknown variant `records`, expected `structured` or `markdown` ``, so the document-record payload is reachable only under the `structured` spelling
rulings.recorded_behavior: `format: "records"` is the document-record payload's name, matching `norn get --format records`, and returns the ordinary `{records, section_failures, notes}` envelope with `isError: false`; `structured` is gone and now fails as the unknown variant, naming `records` / `markdown` as the accepted values
rulings.surface: mcp tools/call vault.get (format param vocabulary)

rulings.prior_behavior: each verb spells an unresolvable target its own way: `set` and `edit` refuse `error: doc not found: <t>`, `get` notes `'<t>' did not resolve to any doc`, and MCP `vault.set` carries `doc not found: <t>` inside its refused report — none of them saying what the target was matched against
rulings.recorded_behavior: every verb refuses with the one resolver wording, `no document matched path or stem: <t>`, built by the single constructor in `crates/norn-core/src/target.rs` and naming the resolution ladder (exact path, then case-insensitive stem) so a reader can tell a typo from an unresolvable alias; codes (`target-not-found`), exit codes (2 for the mutation refusals, 1 for `get`'s error note), stdout payloads, and write-free behavior are unchanged
rulings.surface: target-resolution refusal wording (set / edit / get / mcp vault.set — records, json, and mcp frames)
